name: v1.3 method on all Florida counties in Bauer, Golden and Antonacci territories; Top 150
notes: Same weights, land screen, options and thresholds as v1.3. County-to-manager assignment read from the Feb 2026 7-Eleven team map by Claude (inferred where the map names regions, not counties). Polk kept from the pilot (east of US-27 is McDonald's). Bradford included whole (only east of US-301 is Bauer's). Wakulla, Taylor, Union, Hamilton and Lafayette are not named on the map and are left out. DeSoto left out for now: the DOR 2026 final tax roll (NAL) file for DeSoto is not posted on the DOR portal (checked 2026-11-23). Miami-Dade: 39.5% of target parcels (mostly condo units) don't match the parcel map, so its new-home counts are understated.

scope_approved: Ross, 2026-11-23: run the model on all counties in the Golden, Bauer and Antonacci territories (Florida only); about 3x the pilot population, so a Top 150 instead of a Top 50.
territory_source: 7-Eleven FL-Southeast Development Team Map, Feb 2026 (project file)
changes_line: 1. Same method as the Nov 23 Top 50 (v1.3), now run on every Florida county in Bauer's, Golden's and Antonacci's territories (55 counties, about 19 million people) instead of the 9 pilot counties, so the list is a Top 150. 2. Highway plays list is up to 45. 3. 'By Manager' tab counts areas and corners per 7-Eleven real estate manager and county. 4. County-to-manager assignment is read from 7-Eleven's Feb 2026 team map; Polk stays in (east of US-27 is McDonald's); Bradford is in whole (only east of US-301 is Bauer's). DeSoto is out: DOR hasn't posted its 2026 tax roll. Wakulla, Taylor, Union, Hamilton and Lafayette aren't on the map and are out.
extra_limits: • New markets: 33 of the 150 areas are 10+ miles from any 7-Eleven, mostly in the Panhandle (Bay, Escambia, Leon, Okaloosa, Walton), where 7-Eleven has only 2 stores in our data (Gadsden, Santa Rosa) and 1 recent sale in the tracker (Milton, 2026). The gap score gives full credit at 5+ miles, so these rank high; the 'New market' column flags them. • Miami-Dade new-home counts are understated (39.5% of new residential parcels, mostly condo units, don't match the parcel map). • DeSoto is not included (no 2026 tax roll posted).
